overall_answer: Across the ten briefs, With RAG was preferred in eight reviews (b01–b05, b08–b10); Without RAG was preferred in two (b06–b07). RAG generally made designs more constraint-led, spatially specified, and tailored to audience/venue. Its gains were uneven: some came directly from retrieved cards, some were original elaboration, and RAG also imported unsuitable defaults and did not reliably prevent internal contradictions.

q1_differences.difference: With RAG more often translated the brief into explicit build and safety constraints; Without RAG more often supplied imaginative mechanics or cleaner, simpler concepts.
q1_differences.evidence: With RAG was more spatially/build specific in b02 (coordinates, clearance, exit protection), b03 (hazard/prop counts), b08 (hazard radii and spacing), and b10 (doors, starts, no-lane-cutting). Without RAG was stronger on egg-hatching spectacle in b01, clue discovery in b02, and compact race scope in b10.

q1_differences.difference: RAG more frequently calibrated complexity to vulnerable or novice players, usually reducing hazards, pressure, or required stops.
q1_differences.evidence: b01 reduced the preschool route to four checkpoints and one hazard; b05 used five spacious shared stops; b09 added balance/readability observation and a seated alternative. In contrast, Without RAG was preferred where RAG added inappropriate pressure or complexity: b06’s 1.5-second queen timing and b07’s culturally awkward scored blessing stop.

q1_differences.difference: RAG more often produced explicit thematic and cultural guardrails, but did not consistently apply them appropriately.
q1_differences.evidence: b04 preserved Mae Nak as a village/love-story spirit-release premise and excluded sacred objects as gameplay; b07 included virtual-water/dry-booth safety. Yet b07 turned elder blessing into a mandatory scored checkpoint, while b04 still failed to diagram two non-crossing physical routes.

q1_differences.difference: Without RAG sometimes had better coherence, pacing, or core-game focus; RAG documents still contained cross-stage contradictions.
q1_differences.evidence: Without RAG won b06 through a readable chess-planning ramp and b07 through duration/route consistency. RAG weaknesses include b03’s two-versus-four hazard mismatch, b05’s morning-versus-afternoon art conflict, b07’s 150-second versus three-minute conflict, and b08’s nominal five-minute session ending near 2:20.

q2_advantages.advantage: Age-appropriate preschool pacing in a constrained living room.
q2_advantages.evidence: b01’s four-stop, one-hazard structure was preferred over five stops and two hazards for first-time 5–6-year-olds. Retrieved living-room/family cards recommend a short 4–5-stop loop and designing for the youngest; the family card also supports 1–2 hazards.

q2_advantages.advantage: Build-ready educational route, factual labels, and safe circulation in the gym.
q2_advantages.evidence: b02’s explicit planet facts, 1.5–3 m spacing, eight ordered planets, and not-to-scale framing closely match the solar-system and educator cards. Exact normalized coordinates, spectator orientation, and exit-protection language are valuable but are not supplied by those cards.

b03’s 1.2 m route, 0.6 m margin, fast 2-minute booth framing, and public-activation fit align with venue/size cards. The claimed four hazards and 18–24 props are not directly established by the retrieved cards, and the prototype map contradicts the four-hazard build plan.

q2_advantages.advantage: Closer Mae Nak story, respectful cultural treatment, and paced emotional arc.
q2_advantages.evidence: b04’s village, stilt-house, canal, cradle, Mae Nak helper role, and exclusion of playable sacred objects are strongly supported by the Mae Nak and respectful-Thai-folklore cards. The early-forgiving / dense-middle / calm-return pacing resembles the retrieved runner-flow guidance, though the final five-minute structure is an adaptation rather than a direct template.

b05’s five spacious stops, no pressure, calm garden treatment, and slow scenic moments are directly supported by the seniors/calm-tour cards, which recommend five stops, no time limit, wide spacing, and pauses such as pond or windmill moments.

q2_advantages.advantage: Replay and stream-performance layer for the PC chess game.
q2_advantages.evidence: b06’s clean-run timer, restart loop, and leaderboard fit the retrieved PC-gamers card’s speedrun option and challenge/expression framing. This is a real RAG-derived advantage, but it did not outweigh the damage to the requested cerebral puzzle focus from the 1.5-second final beat.

q2_advantages.advantage: Explicit dry-zone and no-real-water headset safety for Songkran.
q2_advantages.evidence: b07’s separation from real splashing water and dry-booth rule directly follows the retrieved Songkran no-real-water card.

q2_advantages.advantage: Tiny-room dimensions that are concrete enough to implement and test.
q2_advantages.evidence: b08’s four checkpoints, approximately 0.35 m stationary hazards, 0.6 m spawn circle, and 0.5–1 m spacing directly match the tiny-room cards.

q2_advantages.advantage: More concrete senior accessibility checks and alternative access path.
q2_advantages.evidence: b09’s observations of shuffling, reaching for walls/staff, readability, and a seated computer alternative closely match the seniors, seated-alternative, and senior-first-time playtest cards. The return-to-friends/memory-sharing ending is a useful addition but is only loosely related to the retrieved cross-generational social card.

q2_advantages.advantage: Operational six-player safety and authored difficulty ramp.
q2_advantages.evidence: b10’s 8–10-checkpoint two-lane race, walking pace, leaderboard, and spectator side are supported by the Fortal-court card. Separated starts, door clearance, no upward-looking tasks, and its particular nine-checkpoint pacing are useful elaborations, not directly contained in the retrieved cards.

rag_weaknesses.weakness: RAG retrieved or reinforced defaults that conflicted with the brief or the chosen design.
rag_weaknesses.evidence: b07 inherited a 150-second Songkran-booth convention despite a three-minute brief; b05’s retrieved storybook style contains “warm afternoon sun,” producing its morning/afternoon conflict; b01 and b09 retained time-bonus/time-scoring ideas despite calm or untimed positioning.

rag_weaknesses.weakness: RAG did not provide a reliable consistency check across option, prototype, and build-plan stages.
rag_weaknesses.evidence: b03 shows two hazards in the sketch but four in decisions/final plan; b07 has incompatible duration and first-hazard sequencing; b08 promises five minutes but scripts completion at 2:20; b04 promises separate player copies without a two-lane physical diagram.

rag_weaknesses.weakness: Retrieved guidance can be overly generic or mismatched when used without hierarchy and contextual review.
rag_weaknesses.evidence: b06’s RAG replay/speedrun layer was useful but the resulting reflex finale weakened a hard chess-planning brief. b07 used a culturally accurate blessing reference in a competitively scored checkpoint, which the review judged culturally risky.

rag_weaknesses.weakness: RAG did not solve the hardest shared-space feasibility questions.
rag_weaknesses.evidence: b04 lacks measured non-crossing two-player routes; b07 cannot show how four independent 1.2 m courses fit in 10 x 10 m; b10’s prototype sketch still fails to visibly show both lanes.

where_without_rag_was_better.why: It specified a firmer 1.2 m corridor and 0.6 m edge clearance, and had a more vivid egg-hatching climax.
Its clue-based planet discovery was more cognitively engaging, although the actual clue text was missing.
Its two-hazard prototype, sketch, and final plan were internally consistent.
It explicitly required two separate non-crossing lanes for simultaneous players.
It had consistent morning lighting and explicit host-assisted first-time onboarding.
It was the overall winner: clearer chess-planning focus, fairer 3–3.5-second readable beats, a systematic difficulty ramp, and better first-board teaching.
It was the overall winner: correct 180-second duration, more consistent route/hazard specification, and avoided scoring a blessing practice.
Its authored flow occupied nearly the whole intended five-minute session and better conveyed the requested zombie-siege atmosphere.
Its prototype supplied the more exact route coordinates, audience zones, radii, and return loop.
Its seven-checkpoint race was more compact, feasible, and naturally replayable than RAG’s busy nine-checkpoint version.

q3_improvements.improvement: Add a cross-stage constraint and consistency validator before finalizing any design.
q3_improvements.why: Contradictions are the most recurrent RAG failure and can invalidate otherwise strong ideas: b01/b09 time scoring, b03 hazard counts, b05 lighting, b07 duration/route order, b08 session length, and b10 lane depiction.
q3_improvements.how_to_test: For each brief, automatically compare option, prototype, sketch, flow, HUD, and build plan for duration, checkpoint/hazard counts, scoring, lighting, route width, and player count. Require zero unresolved conflicts before human review.

q3_improvements.improvement: Add a feasibility/layout solver for multi-player MR, producing a measured diagram rather than prose promises.
q3_improvements.why: The reviews repeatedly flag unproven simultaneous-play layouts in b04, b07, and b10; this is a safety issue, not merely documentation quality.
q3_improvements.how_to_test: Given room boundary, obstacles, doors, spectators, player count, 1.2 m paths, and 0.6 m margins, generate lanes and collision envelopes. Reject or reduce simultaneous-player count when no valid placement exists; validate with walking-speed trials using the intended number of participants.

q3_improvements.improvement: Rank retrieved cards by brief fit and enforce negative constraints, rather than blending all retrieved defaults.
q3_improvements.why: RAG imported 150-second Songkran timing into b07, afternoon lighting into b05, speedrun pressure into b06, and time bonuses into calm/untimed b01 and b09 experiences.
q3_improvements.how_to_test: Create counterfactual prompt sets: baseline retrieval versus ranked retrieval with explicit exclusions such as “no timer,” “not a competitive ritual,” or “cerebral rather than reflex challenge.” Blind-review resulting designs for brief fit and contradiction rate.

q3_improvements.improvement: Make retrieval provenance claim-level and distinguish card-derived instructions from model-created elaboration.
q3_improvements.why: Exact coordinates in b02, prop/hazard counts in b03, and operational controls in b10 were valuable but not directly present in cards. Attribution otherwise overstates what RAG caused.
q3_improvements.how_to_test: Require each material final-plan field to cite a card ID or “model elaboration.” Independently audit a sample of fields against card text and measure precision of the citations.

q3_improvements.improvement: Add audience-specific playtests as mandatory gates, with outcome thresholds tied to the brief.
q3_improvements.why: The reviews identify unresolved fit risks: b01 child movement load, b05 pair-width/onboarding, b06 puzzle fairness, b08 five-minute pacing, and b09 senior balance/readability.
q3_improvements.how_to_test: Run 5–8 representative users per affected segment. Example thresholds: zero boundary contacts for b01/b05/b09; at least 80% complete b06 without reflex-timing complaints; median b08 first-session engagement near five minutes; no b09 participant reaches for a wall without staff intervention.

caveats: This is a comparison of ten paired outputs from one model and one workflow, not a randomized evaluation across models, prompts, designers, or real players.
The evidence consists of expert blind reviews of documents, not usability studies, implementation results, injury data, learning outcomes, or cultural consultation.
The reviewers’ preferences are high-confidence but qualitative; “preferred” does not establish effect size or statistical significance.
Cards were supplied only for With RAG runs, so a traceable match shows plausible influence, not proof that retrieval caused the feature or that Without RAG could not independently produce it.
Some retrieved cards themselves contain defaults that conflict with individual briefs; a card match is not automatically evidence of good design.
Several conclusions rely on documentation completeness. A missing coordinate, clue, or layout in a brief may have existed in an unstated implementation rather than being absent from the actual game.
